EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by aliphatic C–H stretches at 2937 / 2887 cm⁻¹ and strong CH₃/CH₂ bending at 1454 cm⁻¹, indicating a saturated alkyl chain.  A carbonyl-type band appears at 1658 cm⁻¹; this is too low for a ketone or carboxylic acid (≈1710–1740 cm⁻¹) but matches the amide-I C=O stretch (≈1640–1670 cm⁻¹).  Supporting amide fingerprints are present: the amide-III/C–N band at 1281 cm⁻¹ and another C–N stretch near 1048 cm⁻¹.  No strong nitro (1300–1550 cm⁻¹) or aldehyde C–H (around 2820 cm⁻¹) doublet is observed, and there is no peak in the 1710 cm⁻¹ region required for candidates containing carboxyl or ketone groups.  Only Candidate 1 (CCNC(=O)CC(C)C) contains a secondary amide functional group together with the observed aliphatic environment, making it the most consistent with the experimental Raman peaks.
